title: Baking soda misuse as a home remedy: case experience of the California Poison Control System
journal: Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics
followUp: Retrospective review of cases reported from 2000 to 2012
population: Symptomatic cases of ingestion and misuse of a baking soda powder product reported to the California Poison Control System; ages 2 months to 79 years; 55.8% female
funder: Not read: the full text is restricted to subscribers; only the abstract page was read, in an Internet Archive copy.
result: Of 192 cases, the most common reasons for misuse were antacid use (60.4%), attempts to 'beat a urine drug test' (11.5%) and treatment of urinary tract infection (4.7%). 55.2% had significant symptoms warranting medical evaluation; 12 patients required hospital admission and developed electrolyte imbalances, metabolic alkalosis or respiratory depression.
